svg.text: Trafag Italia - item cost in SAP B1: what we found
Schema it01_p, read-only query, 2026-07-28 | Context: group margin reporting | Key point: this is expected B1 behaviour, not a data error
1. Valuation method today
OITM.EvalSystem, active inventory items only (InvntItem = 'Y' AND validFor = 'Y'), approx. 31,900 items
B = Batch / Serial
approx. 31,600 items = 99.1 %
A = Moving Average
(this is what group policy asks for)
S = Standard
6 items = 0.02 %
Verified, not assumed: all 39,582 items with EvalSystem = 'B' are batch- or serial-managed
(ManBtchNum = 'Y' on 39,581, ManSerNum = 'Y' on 1) - a 100 % match, no exceptions.
2. Where the cost value actually sits
Two different levels in B1 - this is the core of the misunderstanding we had
Item master - EMPTY
OITM.AvgPrice / OITM.PrdStdCst / OITW.AvgPrice
0 of the 31,600 batch-valued items carry a value.
Expected: under batch valuation B1 keeps the cost per batch,
not in the item master. These fields will never fill up.
Document line - POPULATED
INV1.StockPrice (sales invoice line)
2,019 of 2,082 materials sold in 2026 have a cost = approx. 97 %.
Example item 56746: 86 invoice lines, all with a cost, avg. 27.91 EUR
- while the item master shows 0.00 for the same item.
3. What we do right now (approved by Andreas as a first step - no action needed from you)
TR IT sells a material
B1 posts the actual cost of the
batch onto the invoice line
INV1.StockPrice
We import that daily
already part of the existing
finance data feed - nothing new
has to be delivered
Group margin view
uses it as Trafag Italia's own
cost basis - same principle we
already use for CH/AT in SAP
Coverage limit
Only covers materials TR IT sells
itself. Materials only passed on
without an own sale have no value.
4. What we would like you to check
Group policy calls for Moving Average valuation. Based on section 1 that does not seem to be rolled out in Italy yet.
Question 1 - switching the method
What would need to change in B1 to move Italy's
inventory items to Moving Average valuation,
in line with group policy?
Note: batch management and batch valuation are two
different settings. 215 items already use Moving Average
valuation while still being batch-managed - so the two
do not necessarily have to change together.
Question 2 - is a cost run needed?
Would a one-time cost run (inventory revaluation)
be required to populate average costs for the
existing stock after such a switch?
For reference: of the 296 items already on Moving Average
today, 224 (approx. 76 %) have an average cost populated.
We cannot tell from the data alone whether a method switch
would be enough on its own - that is where we need you.
Please note
Nothing in section 1 or 2 is a data quality problem on your side - a batch-valued item legitimately has no item-master cost.
The short-term reporting need is already solved (section 3). Section 4 is about aligning Italy with the group valuation policy, where Andreas offers his support.
Item counts move by a few units between queries because items are created continuously in the live system - all figures are approximate.
Source: read-only SELECT against it01_p on BI1 (OITM, OITW, OINV/INV1), 2026-07-27 and 2026-07-28. Contact: Ingo Kohler, IT Analytics.
